name: Possible potting turntable at Tell Feres al-Sharqi
description: A small clay disc with a slight socket was found in the Late Ubaid potters’ workshop at Tell Feres in north-eastern Syria. Its shape is consistent with a pivot-mounted support used in pottery work. The forming marks that indicate sustained rotary motion appear in later deposits.

date.label: ca. 4700 BCE, Late Ubaid workshop
date.basis: The original comparative study places the workshop discovery in the local Late Ubaid phase at about 4700 BCE.

events.statement: A clay disc about 26 cm in diameter with a shallow possible pivot socket was recovered in the pottery workshop.

evidence.supports: Describes and dates the disc and discusses possible rotary use.
Documents potting equipment with the excavated workshop, including possible turntable disc fragments.

events.caveats: Its interpretation as a turntable is provisional. This is workshop context dating.

earliest_record.rationale: Context of the recovered disc, with its inferred function stated separately.

unresolved.note: Compare bearing wear and rotation marks on the clay disc with the later wheel-coiling sequence, including intervening contexts.
